title: CS4: Measuring the Creativity of Large Language Models Automatically by Controlling the Number of Story-Writing Constraints
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to evaluate the creativity of large language models in story writing. The authors argue that existing benchmarks are inadequate because broad prompts allow models to reproduce or lightly adapt memorized narratives from training data, making it hard to distinguish genuine creativity from retrieval-like behavior. To address this, they define creativity as producing original, unseen, high-quality stories and propose a benchmark that increases prompt specificity by adding many story-writing constraints.

The intervention introduced is CS4, a benchmark for constrained story generation. CS4 synthesizes prompts with 7, 15, 23, 31, or 39 constraints using two methods: an instruction-based approach and a story-based approach. The authors then generate a base story with GPT-4 and ask several 7B models (including LLaMA-2, Gemma, Mistral, and OLMo variants) to revise the base story to satisfy the constraints. The resulting stories are evaluated automatically using LLM judges on constraint satisfaction, coherence, grammar, likability, and diversity, and the paper proposes new creativity metrics based on quality under increasing numbers of constraints and performance decay as constraints increase.

The paper does not study students, teachers, or educational settings. Its empirical context is NLP/AI benchmarking using synthesized prompts and model-generated stories, with experiments conducted on 500 prompts and 3,000 generated stories. The work is situated as a general evaluation framework for model creativity rather than a human-subjects intervention.

The main conclusions are that all tested LLMs perform worse as prompts become more specific, but the rate of decline differs across models. Gemma-7B and Mistral-7B show stronger performance under high constraint loads than LLaMA-2 and OLMo variants, and Gemma shows the slowest degradation, which the authors interpret as greater creativity. The paper also concludes that learning from human feedback improves performance mainly when prompts have fewer constraints, with benefits shrinking substantially as constraint load increases. Overall, the authors present CS4 as a low-cost automatic benchmark for indirectly measuring originality in LLM story writing.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark/model-evaluation paper on LLM story generation, not a causal or quasi-experimental study of an educational intervention in K-12 settings. It does not evaluate student learning outcomes, uses no school-age sample, and appears to be an arXiv preprint rather than peer-reviewed education evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: No K-12 literacy or other student outcomes are measured, so there is no direct evidence of educational impact. Reported results concern model performance metrics such as constraint satisfaction, coherence, and diversity rather than effects on learners.

interventions.use_case: Benchmarking large language models for constrained story-writing creativity and instruction-following under increasing prompt specificity; not an educational intervention or K-12 instructional tool evaluation.
